title: Blood-brain-barrier and white matter mechanisms underlying dementia
text:
White matter damage has increasingly been recognized as an important contributing factor to neurodegeneration
and the two most severe types of dementia: Alzheimer’s disease and vascular cognitive impaired dementia. The
work proposed here will address a novel pericyte mediated signaling pathway as the underlying molecular and
cellular mechanisms for white matter pathology induced by chronic hypoperfusion which may have therapeutic
implication.

title: Integrative Center for Environmental Microbiomes and Human Health
text:
Microbiomes, critical to human health and functioning, are embedded within and are influenced by
environmental context. By gaining a deeper understanding of how microbial variation affects human health, we
can devise holistic strategies to promote a sustainable, resilient biosphere.

title: Novel gene discovery in disorders of the liver and biliary tree
text:
Because our understanding of hepatobiliary disease is incomplete, a significant number of children with biliary
tree dysgenesis and liver disease have nondiagnostic genetic testing. The goal of this research proposal is to
improve the diagnosis and care of children and adults with liver and biliary disease by better characterizing the
genetic landscape of these conditions. To accomplish this goal, we will assemble and characterize a large cohort
of patients with biliary and liver disease and apply a research pipeline for gene discovery and validation, with
additional focus on MED12 as a novel biliary dysgenesis gene.

title: Natural Language Processing Based Consultation Feedback to Improve Patient Decision Making and Physician Risk Communication
text:
We plan a cluster randomized controlled trial testing whether providing patients and physicians with natural
language processing (NLP)-based feedback along with artificial intelligence (AI) summaries of what was said
about key risks and rewards of treatment options improves patient decision making and physician risk
communication compared to standard of care counseling along with American Urological Association-
endorsed educational materials in men with prostate cancer. Our cluster randomized trial will test whether our
intervention affects decisional conflict, shared decision making, and appropriateness of treatment on the
patient level (Aim 1) and quality of risk communication on the physician level (Aim 2). We will then examine
variation in quality of risk communication across subgroups of tumor risk, physician specialty, and race in the
control arm to identify populations at risk for poor risk communication (Aim 3).

title: From intra to intercellular regulatory networks that define cell type identity
text:
Cell fate engineering, for example the directed differentiation of pluripotent stem cells or
the direct conversion among somatic cell types, holds great promise to improve disease
modeling, drug screening, and to lead to regenerative medicine therapies. However, our
ability to engineering cell fate with fidelity has been impeded by an incomplete
understanding of the biological networks that govern development. In this work, I propose
to address this problem through a combination of algorithm development and data
generation, with an emphasis on cell types related to the synovial joint.

title: Combinatorial effects of PTMs on a-Synuclein structure function and aggregation
text:
The aggregation of α-Synuclein into fibrillar aggregates plays a pivotal role in the progression of Parkinson’s
Disease and related neurodegenerative disorders. The proposed research will create α-Synuclein modified by
chemical groups identified in post-mortem tissues and test the impact of these modifications both on functional
and dysfunctional interactions of the protein. This research will provide insight into the relationship between the
structural effects of these modifications on α-Synuclein and disease propagation.

title: Regulation of intestinal lipid metabolism by type-3 immune cytokine
text:
Malnutrition and metabolic imbalance are prevalent comorbidities of bowel inflammation, frequently associated
with poor clinical outcomes. However, managing these complications is challenging, and current therapies are
ineffective, due to critical gaps in understanding the connection between the inflammatory environment and the
absorptive enterocyte function. This proposal aims to bridge these gaps by elucidating how mucosal immune
effector impacts enterocyte nutrient uptake and systemic metabolism, potentially uncovering new ways to treat
nutrient imbalance associated with inflammation and digestive disorders.

title: Interrogating MRCK Protein Kinases in Ovarian Cancer
text:
High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is the deadliest form of ovarian cancer due to frequent
recurrence and metastasis with minimal treatment options. Recurrent HGSOC often spreads to the peritoneal
cavity in the form of ascites, where tumor cells grow as spheroids, and metastasize to other organs causing
death. The overall goal of this proposal is to uncover how protein kinases orchestrate this process, so that we
can design kinase inhibitor therapies to prevent the growth and spread of recurrent HGSOC.

title: Multi-omics Gene Network Identification (Project 4)
text: The goal of Project 4 is to discover neurobiologically interpretable gene networks that underlie opioid addiction (OA) but are otherwise missed by traditional statistical approaches. To achieve this goal, we will apply our multi-omics, multi-method framework—Gene Network Identification and Integration (GNetII)—to identify OA-associated gene networks, by capitalizing on P50 data across human and rodent models. GNetII includes genome-wide epistasis, explainable artificial intelligence, gene network construction, and lines-of- evidence (LOE) methods. These cornerstone methods enable integration of multiple levels of individual-level data, and we will specifically integrate large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) data in 220,722 living subjects from Project 1 and the Synergy Core, gene regulation data (RNA-sequencing, DNA methylation, chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, and variant genotypes) from multiple addiction- relevant brain tissues (including prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, and amygdala) from 641 OA case and control decedents (deceased individuals) from Project 2, experimental mouse and rat model results from Project 3, and additional public omics data. OA is a leading cause of preventable morbidity and mortality in the United States, afflicting an unprecedented number of U.S. adults and youth. OA is highly heritable (~54%). Yet, few genetic loci have been conclusively identified for OA and related outcomes, and common genetic variant-based heritability explains only 17% of the variance in OA. We hypothesize that epistasis (i.e., interaction of variants or genes) contributes to the missing heritability. Applying big data science methods to large-scale GWAS, gene regulation data in brain tissue, and cross-species data will reveal previously undetected relationships and add knowledge of the neurobiology underlying addiction. We propose the following specific aims: Aim 1: Build OA-associated gene networks via genome-wide epistasis. Aim 2: Build multi-omics networks using postmortem human brain data. Aim 3: Integrate networks across species to find OA-associated gene networks with multiple LOE. Analyses will be performed on the powerful high performance computing architectures at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory which will greatly improve the likelihood of neurobiologically meaningful discoveries. Our study will capture complex networks across the genome to find previously unknown genes and will help explain the neurobiological underpinnings for the genetic loci that emerge from across the P50 and the broader field.

title: Keys to prevent iron hijacking and infection by intracellular pathogenic bacteria
text:
Importance to public health: An emerging tick-borne disease, human granulocytic anaplasmosis, is caused by
infection with Anaplasma phagocytophilum, which is an obligatory intracellular bacterium. The purpose of this
project is to understand how A. phagocytophilum acquire host iron and overcome host nutritional immunity in
order to infect human cells and cause disease. Ultimately, our results will fill a key knowledge gap in the field of
Anaplasma molecular pathogenesis via a thorough understanding of biomolecular mechanisms involved in
intracellular iron uptake by Anaplasma, host cell innate immune responses, and consequent disease.
Relevance to NIH’s mission: Our work pertains to developing fundamental knowledge that will reduce the
burden of human disability caused by infectious disease.

title: BLR&D Research Career Scientist Award Application
text:
The demographics of the veteran population clearly demonstrate that illnesses that afflict the elderly
are a major concern of the Department of Veterans Affairs. Currently, the number of veterans over 60 years of
age represents over 50% of the total veteran population. It is noteworthy that the number of veterans 80 years
and older is projected to increase 500% over the next 20 years. Research has shown that chronic, low-grade
inflammation increases dramatically with age and that inflammation is a major risk factor for a variety of age-
related diseases that affect elderly veterans, e.g., Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s diseases, atherosclerosis,
diabetes, cancer, frailty, etc. Dr. Richardson’s current research will be the first to study the effect of necroptosis
on the age-related increase in chronic inflammation and will be translationally important because this research
could potentially lead to therapies that reduce age-related diseases and improve the health of elderly veterans.

title: Regulatory mechanisms governing imprinted domains during early development
text:
Epigenetic mechanisms that govern imprinted domain regulation are complex. We have discovered a novel,
nucleoporin mechanism of imprinted domain regulation, and having identified other factors involved in
imprinting, we can now build upon this mechanism to understand how imprinted domain are regulated during
early development. Data from this proposal will contribute to our understanding of how disruptions in imprinting
can impact development and lead to imprinting disorders.

title: Enhancing cytotoxic lymphocytes in a TB vaccine strategy
text:
Tuberculosis remains among the most common causes of death from an
infectious disease worldwide. This proposal will test a novel “enhanced prime and pull” strategy
designed to enhance the efficacy of the current BCG vaccine against tuberculosis.

title: Discovery of cancer-specific surface protein conformations in acute myeloid leukemia and de novo design of highly selective binders in pursuit of improved immunotherapies
text:
Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a devasting disease, representing one of the most common adult leukemias
and carrying a dismal 5-year survival of ~30%. Therapies harnessing the immune system (“immunotherapies”)
have been very effective versus other blood cancers but have largely failed to show benefit in AML. Here, we
aim to address this challenge by identifying a new class of immunotherapy targets and validating potential ther-
apies against them, with the long-term goal of providing new treatment options for AML patients desperately in
need.

title: Optimizing Use of Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) to Improve Care for Youth with Type 1 Diabetes
text:
The use of personal medical devices (e.g. continuous glucose monitors) by youth with type 1 diabetes as well
as their potential to aid children and their caregivers to manage the daily demands of type 1 diabetes and
optimize blood sugar control have rapidly expanded over the past twenty years. However, demographic (e.g.
race/ethnicity) and socioeconomic (e.g. household income, parental education, and insurance) factors impact
access to and continued use of such technology. The goals of this project are to better describe and analyze
the interplay of such factors in sustained utilization of CGM in different clinical settings and to characterize their
impact on a national level to enable the development and implementation of a pilot study designed to achieve
improvement in continuous glucose monitoring use for pediatric patients with type 1 diabetes.

title: Discovery of novel antivirulence drug targets in C. difficile by systematically demystifying its genetic network controlling toxin biosynthesis
text:
Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a leading cause of hospital-acquired diarrhea due to dysbiosis caused by
broad-spectrum antibiotics. Cellular pathways affecting toxin biosynthesis is promising for anti-virulence drugs
that spare the beneficial gut microbiota. This proposal seeks to identify and characterize drug targets within such
pathways, from which to develop anti-virulence drugs for CDI.

title: UC Irvine MODEL-AD
text:
Understanding the complexity of the development of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and developing and testing
effective therapeutics and interventions requires the generation of animal models that faithfully recapitulate the
disease. We have spent five years creating the individual components that we will now combine to produce
mice that develop relevant aspects of AD. Furthermore, we will carry out deep phenotyping of these mice
across their lifespans and align their pathologies and gene expression profiles with human signatures. All mice
and data will be made freely available to all investigators, in academia and industry alike, so that the global
research field can use these resources to develop and test therapeutics and ultimately combat AD.

title: Cellular Thermogenesis and Lifespan Modulation: Mechanisms of Cold-Temperature Aging in Drosophila
text:
Cold temperatures dramatically extend lifespan in fruit flies, but the underlying biological mechanisms remain
unknown. This project will investigate how cold triggers beneficial changes in metabolism, nutrient sensing, and
protein quality control that work together to slow aging. Understanding these processes could uncover new
strategies to promote healthy aging in humans.

title: AI-Powered Quantitative Analysis of Sinus CT Scans for Enhanced Clinical Assessment and Research
text:
Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) affects millions of Americans and leads to substantial healthcare costs and reduced
quality of life. This project will create an automated, cloud-based toolkit that transforms routine sinus CT scans
into standardized, quantitative measures of disease severity and airflow physiology. In parallel, the project will
actively involve undergraduate and master’s students in biomedical imaging and AI research, preparing a diverse
next generation of scientists while advancing tools that can improve CRS diagnosis, treatment evaluation, and
public health outcomes.

title: Identifying Nursing Models of Care to Improve Emergency Department Patient Outcomes
text:
PROJECTIVE NARRATIVE
This study will leverage nursing models of care to advance better patient outcomes with a focus on reducing
patient outcome disparities in the safety net of the U.S. healthcare system—hospital emergency departments
(EDs). The outcomes from this study will address a key objective of Healthy People 2030 to improve care in
EDs where timely care is essential for improving health outcomes. This study has strong public health
relevance given the focus on hospital EDs as important care settings in communities that provide a large
proportion of care for under- and un-insured patients as well as racial and ethnic minorities.
